transcript:
The testim[en]t dative & Inv[en]tar of the gudis geir soumes
of money & dettis p[er]tein[in]g to umq[uhi]le Johne glasgw in hirmenschelis

surname_quote: Margaret's surname could be hochame, but personally I see hochaine as more the likely possibility. Hochaine may be a phonetic variant of the surname Hutchin.
owner_reply: Thank you, that makes a lot of sense actually as there's a connection to the Hutcheson family in that period!
owner_name_question: Interesting, would be an unusual name - no other Marjory's until the 1900s. Does it maybe say Marion instead? With a long “n” + a terminal loop?
name_reply: I'm fairly confident that it reads "m[ar]iory", though of course I could be wrong. Even though I'm open to other possibilities, I definitely don't see Marion-- there are far too many strokes for the last letter to be simply "n" for one thing, and on top of that if this were Marion then the terminal loop would need to be decorative-- not something I've seen from this writer anywhere else. On the other hand, Margery/Marjory wasn't that rare a name in this period-- in fact, it was often used interchangeably with Margaret, which makes sense considering that was her mother's name.

assessment.label: Widow's surname
assessment.text: The contributor prefers hochaine, with hochame as an alternative. This differs from the site's earlier Hoghame and Cochrane suggestions. Hochaine is now included prominently as a human reading, rather than silently normalizing the manuscript to a modern surname.

assessment.label: Hutchin / Hutcheson lead
assessment.text: The contributor proposes that Hochaine may be a phonetic variant of Hutchin. The project owner's reply connects this suggestion with Hutcheson-family research. This is a useful surname and family-network hypothesis, not confirmation that Margaret belongs to a particular Hutchin or Hutcheson family.

assessment.label: The child's name
assessment.text: The accepted reading is m[ar]iory, modernized as Marjory. Double_Show_9316 initially writes m[ar]jory and then explains m[ar]iory, rejecting Marion on the final strokes and terminal loop. The project owner accepts this human correction and notes that the initial a required by the earlier model reading is unsupported. Androw is superseded, not an equal competing reading.

assessment.label: Relationship boundary
assessment.text: The quoted his relict identifies Margaret as John's widow. The contributor's closing reference to 'her mother's name' is an interpretation, not independent proof that Margaret was the named children's mother. The widow, child and father clauses must be distinguished from an unproved maternity link.

assessment.label: Associated Hutcheson fragment
assessment.text: The purchased PDF also includes a supplementary view labelled Image 276, showing a strip marked 396A with the confirmation of Andro Hutchesoun (exact spelling provisional). Its deliberate delivery with John's image should not be dismissed as an accident. The human Hochaine/Hutchin proposal makes it a worthwhile family-network lead, but no explicit link to Margaret or John is securely read so far. The fragment's children and Johne clauses need a separate transcription, and its original attachment needs archival clarification.

accepted_reading.basis: Supplied human transcription accepted by the project owner
